clue.text: As a student one loveless 0 plutocrat curtailed fairy's seeing things were OK

parts.note: qua is Latin for 'as', 'in the capacity of'
L, the learner plate, stands for a student
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: love is nil, O in tennis scores, so loveless says one O is taken away

parts.note: a tycoon is a rich and powerful businessman

indicators.note: curtailed means the tail, the last letter, is cut off

parts.note: a troll is a creature of Scandinavian fairy tale

explanation.surface: A rich student, short of love, has fairy visions and decides all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' takes one O from TYCOON to leave TYCON; 'curtailed' cuts the last L off TROLL to leave TROL. The stray '0' in the held text is a print mark and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspection that checks products meet a standard is what makes sure things are all right.

clue.text: Whole ruined — see within

indicators.note: within says the word for see sits inside the word for ruined

parts.note: to undo someone is to ruin them, so ruined gives undid
vide is the Latin 'see', used in references

explanation.surface: Someone surveys a scene of total destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' marks the container; 'see' is the Latin vide of footnotes and cross-references, and 'ruined' is the past tense of undo in its sense of bringing to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not split into parts is entire and complete.

clue.text: Primate at the wall of Paris

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
mur is French for wall, the language a Parisian speaks

explanation.surface: A monkey perched on one of the old city walls of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Paris' says both pieces are French: LE MUR is 'the wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: This ring-tailed Madagascar animal belongs to the order of monkeys and apes.

clue.text: Majority once departed in Power right away

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Majority once departed in Power right away (6-3)': the wordplay T(WENT)YONE needs TYRONE (the actor Tyrone Power) with R away, and the word Tyrone is missing from the held text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Majority once departed in Power right away

clue.text: Two and two with a drink

indicators.note: a second two alongside the first says the same piece is written twice

parts.note: two's company, so two gives CO, the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Two couples share a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'two's company' turns 'two' into CO, the abbreviation for company, and 'and two' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate beverage made from ground cacao beans.

clue.text: Inaccurate locating's due to yearning for the past

indicators.note: inaccurate says the letters are not in their right places and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A satnav that gets places wrong leaves a driver longing for the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'locating's' is part of the fodder: all nine letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wistful about earlier times is the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Send for the scope of authority

definitions.meaning: to send money or refer a matter
the range of tasks someone is authorised to handle

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means dispatching payment; as a noun it is the brief or terms of reference given to a person or body.

clue.text: Marathon for the Mousetrap?

definitions.meaning: a marathon is a race of great distance
Agatha Christie's play The Mousetrap has run in London since 1952

explanation.walkthrough: The Mousetrap is Agatha Christie's murder mystery, playing in London's West End since 1952, the longest continuous run of any play.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a lengthy race on foot, and a play staged for decades enjoys an extended theatrical engagement.

clue.text: One cross on another is meant to be charming

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first cross comes before the second

parts.note: one gives the article A
a mule is a cross between a donkey and a horse
another cross, the letter T, which is cross-shaped

explanation.surface: Two crosses stacked together make a lucky charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' is a hybrid animal first (MULE), then a shape (T); 'on' sets MULE above T in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm worn to ward off evil is meant to work magic, a play on 'charming'.

clue.text: Two mothers, one lady?

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A family with two mums asks which one is the lady.
explanation.walkthrough: MA and DAM are both words for mother; together they make a polite address to a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal title for a woman, as in 'Excuse me, ma'am'.

clue.text: Remove island from ous-toms?

parts.note: to excise is to cut out or remove
the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: An instruction to take an island out of the customs regime.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland. 'Customs' is hyphenated across a line in print.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer who collected duties on goods worked for the Customs and Excise service.

clue.text: Inlet permanently given to young runner

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the word let

parts.note: taken as written
ever means always, permanently

explanation.surface: A creek is handed over for good to a young athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inlet' looks like a creek, but must be split as 'In let', with 'In' the container signal. A leveret is a hare in its first year.
explanation.definitionFit: A hare under a year old is a young animal famous for running.

clue.text: It's suitable in a bad road, but it's better to have more sockets

definitions.text: it's better to have more sockets

indicators.note: in says the word for suitable is placed inside the other letters
bad says the letters of road are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: apt means suitable

explanation.surface: A remark about a poor road turns into advice on wiring up more plugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges to make ADOR and 'in' marks the container. The definition is a playful description of a multi-plug, not a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug fitting that lets several devices share one outlet effectively multiplies the points available.

clue.text: Mount Ida looks partly moonstruck

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Greek mountain seems to be under a lunar spell.
explanation.definitionFit: The rise and fall of the sea is driven by the moon's pull, so it is affected by the moon.

clue.text: Loan cures characters with sticky fingers

indicators.note: characters means the letters of the words, to be reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A loan that cures debts attracts people who like to pinch things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' signals the letters of LOAN CURES taken as loose characters and rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone light-fingered is inclined to theft.

clue.text: Round church worker, without energy, to confess needing pruning

parts.note: the round shape of the letter O

indicators.note: without says the letter for energy is dropped

parts.note: a verger is a church caretaker
E is the physics symbol for energy
to own up, to own, is to confess

explanation.surface: A church official goes round confessing his garden needs a trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops one E from VERGER to leave VERGR.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants left to spread too far are in want of cutting back.

clue.text: Ties off before tied knot: if you don't like it, read your meter!

definitions.text: if you don't like it, read your meter!

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second
off means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a couple who have tied the knot have married, or mated

explanation.surface: Advice on ties and knots ends in a gas-bill grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TIES into ESTI. An energy bill not based on a reading is a guess; read your own meter to correct it.
explanation.definitionFit: A utility bill calculated by guesswork rather than a reading is labelled this way.

clue.text: Well-timed work for piano with alternative melody

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
or introduces an alternative
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A piano piece with a choice of tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coming at just the right moment is timely.

clue.text: Suffered a French river in Yorkshire

parts.note: un is French for a
the Derwent is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A French visitor was having a bad time by a northern English river.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire is a county in northern England; the Derwent flows through it.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through an ordeal is to endure it.

clue.text: Reproach for getting out of bed for scrambled eggs?

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
scrambled egg is slang for the gold braid on a senior officer's cap

explanation.surface: Someone is scolded for getting up just to cook scrambled eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambled eggs' wants to be breakfast; it is military slang for gold braid on an officer's peak.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold or rebuke someone is to find fault with them.

clue.text: Fowl not bareheaded?

parts.note: someone not bareheaded has a cap
the cap is on

explanation.surface: A bird that wears a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, CAP ON describes someone not bareheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated cockerel fattened for the table is a domestic bird.

clue.text: An odd letter requires brains

indicators.note: requires here means the phrase holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Working out an unusual letter takes intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'aN ODD LEtter'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for the head, and so for one's wits.

clue.text: The last page describes a hold-up, as it were

definitions.meaning: a support that holds up a row of books

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the words give the close of a volume; whole, they name a shelf support propping volumes upright.

clue.text: Choose 1st century viewer?

parts.note: to opt is to choose
I is the Roman numeral one, as in first
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: Picking out a first-century observer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyepiece or lens on an instrument, or the eye itself, is used for seeing.

clue.text: Get rid of the liquid that laughs

definitions.text: Get rid of the liquid that laughs

parts.words: Get rid of the liquid that laughs
parts.note: to empty out water, and the outlet whose gurgle sounds like laughter

explanation.definitionFit: To pour off water is to empty it away, and a gurgling plughole seems to chuckle.

clue.text: Is the girl a non-violent revolutionary?

parts.note: mild means gentle, not violent
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Asking whether a woman is a peaceful communist.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional female first name.

clue.text: Tuscan city sounds beautiful

indicators.note: sounds says the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a looker is a beautiful person

explanation.surface: An Italian town is said to be lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, with the R silent, LOOKER sounds like LUCCA.
explanation.definitionFit: A walled town in Tuscany, near Pisa.

clue.text: Little boy, as stressed out, definitely a high flier

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: out means the other pieces stand outside the boy, around him

parts.note: something stressed is pulled tight, taut
Ron is a short form of the boy's name Ronald

explanation.surface: A small boy, stressed out, is certainly flying high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stressed out' looks like one phrase, but splits into the word for tense and 'out', the signal that those letters go outside the little boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller flies higher than anyone, literally.

clue.text: Sounds a loose yarn, devoid of kindness

indicators.note: sounds says the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: crewel is a loosely twisted worsted yarn used in embroidery

explanation.surface: A tall tale that is thin on compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a story; it is the embroidery wool CREWEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking compassion is being heartless.

clue.text: The squanderer's bouncing

parts.note: to play this game is to waste money, and the game itself is skimming stones so they bounce on water

explanation.definitionFit: Skimming flat stones across water is a pastime, and 'playing' it with money means wasting it.
